# Project agent memory

This file is the project's committed home for project-intrinsic agent knowledge: build, test, release, architecture, and sharp-edge notes that should travel with the code.

## What this project is

Firstmate 3000 is a local-only Electron desktop app: a calm AI first-officer that routes work to the user's own LLM subscriptions (Codex, Copilot, Grok, Claude Max, Cursor, Kimi, OpenRouter, ...). No SaaS, no hosted backend, no account system from us. Product vision, interaction model, and constraints: `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/readme.md`.

## Standing product principle (captain, 2026-08-17)

FM3000 is the most advanced agent harness, but it aggressively hides that complexity from the end user. The user interacts with just the main Firstmate agent and a few settings - nothing else. The fewer concepts we expose, the better. Accounts, harnesses, crewmate transports, quota routing, and rebinding are machinery; the surfaces a person touches stay calm. Concretely: the sign-in flow and the Subscriptions tab never expose the "harness" technicality - they speak only of providers, accounts (labeled by the user), and quota. An e2e assertion enforces the wording.

## Design system (mandatory)

All UI work MUST follow the project skill `firstmate-3000-design` (`.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/`). It owns every visual and interaction rule: tokens, type, color, motion, components, character rendering, tone of copy. Never re-invent brand rules in code; if a rule is missing, extend the skill first, then implement. The package is offline-complete (fonts and mock runtime vendored; see its readme "Offline completeness").

- Tokens: `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/tokens/*.css` - consume these, never hardcode values they define.
- Click-through mock of the whole app: serve the skill dir over HTTP (any static server), open `ui_kits/firstmate/index.html`. Voice states trigger on a real right-⌥ keydown.

## Architecture and implementation

The architecture is **decided** (captain sign-off 2026-08-13, decision record in `docs/architecture.md` §14 - do not relitigate). Implementers start from `docs/implementation-plan.md`, which orders the build into phases with acceptance checks and names the house reference repos to mirror (Pi SDK, hi-bit, baby-menu, pi-launcher). If reality contradicts a recorded decision, escalate with `needs-decision` instead of improvising. Current build status vs the plan: `docs/mvp-status.md`.

## Working on the code

- Green gate on every commit: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence && pnpm test`, then `pnpm build && pnpm exec playwright test` for the e2e suite. The adherence lint runs the design skill's `_adherence.oxlintrc.json` through ESLint FlatCompat (current oxlint cannot execute its selector rules); its raw-px/hex rules are warn-level by the skill's own design.
- Standing CI rule (PR 8): CI green only if every check on the exact head commit SHA reports status=completed and conclusion=success (use `gh pr checks`). One green `checks` job never suffices while `package-smoke` or others pend/fail. Never treat old SHAs as authoritative for the current head.
- E2E runs are hermetic and windowless: `tests/e2e/launch.ts` gives each app a throwaway userData and HOME (`FM3000_USER_DATA_DIR` keeps the window hidden - captain directive), fake media devices (no macOS mic prompt), a mock OpenAI-compatible provider wired through app-scoped `models.json` (`tests/e2e/mockProvider.ts`), and faked voice-model readiness (opt out with `voiceModelReady: false`). Quota fixtures ride `FM3000_QUOTA_FIXTURE_DIR`. Claude credentials seed into that HOME's `.claude` (`prepareHome`), never a per-account vault store.
- `flag_missed_escalation` (PoC-2 capture C3, `src/core/pi/supervisionTools.ts`) is the only path from "you should have told me about that" to a durable label: under-escalation is otherwise unobservable, because a routine verdict is one feed line and no captain contact. It stamps migration 16's nullable `missed_escalation`/`missed_note`/`missed_at` on the task's newest routine `supervision_outcomes` row (or a named `#id` from `supervision_log`), write-once, `routine`-only, and captain-turn gated by the same wake stamp `remember` uses - the label's value is that the captain confirmed it, so the agent cannot manufacture one on a scheduled or supervision wake. Refusals are tool text, never throws. No card, no setting, no user surface.
- The retrospective miss deriver (PoC-2 capture C2, `scripts/derive-miss-candidates.ts`, `docs/miss-deriver.md`) is an OFFLINE tables-only scan: for every `supervision_outcomes` `routine` verdict it looks forward in a window (default 24h) for a later captain verdict, a host-written `turn_failed` / task-failure wake, a captain-resolved card, or a captain steer/interrupt on that task, and emits weak candidate-miss JSONL. Never writes C3's `missed_escalation`/`missed_note`/`missed_at`. Inputs are parameters (`--db`/`--user-data`/`--window-hours`) so a MacBook-exported `firstmate.db` runs identically. Fixture-tested; no live data required.
- The dispatch extractor (PoC-2 capture C5, `scripts/extract-dispatch-corpus.ts`, `docs/dispatch-extractor.md`) is an OFFLINE dev tool over data the app already writes: Pi session JSONL joined to `tasks`/`repos`/`cards`, emitting the six-way classify-first turns as a weakly-labelled JSONL corpus. No schema change, no product surface, nothing leaves the box. Its inputs are all parameters (`--user-data`/`--sessions`/`--db`) so another machine's exported userData runs identically. C2, C4, and C5 are the `scripts/*.ts` files: Node 24 type-strips them with no build step, which is why their relative imports carry an explicit `.ts` and `tsconfig.node.json` sets `allowImportingTsExtensions`.
- The corpus export (PoC-2 capture C4, `scripts/export-corpus.ts`, `docs/corpus-export.md`) is the one command that packages the capture for an eval/training run: `supervision_outcomes` (C1 provenance + C3's confirmed-miss label) joined to `cards`/`tasks`, plus C5's dispatch records - it CALLS the C5 extractor, never re-implements it. It reuses Observe's gate verbatim (`isDevObserveEnabled`), checked BEFORE any file is read, because it moves transcripts; `detectPackaged` stands in for `app.isPackaged` in a script and `FM3000_PACKAGED=1` can only tighten it. An unflagged routine row is no label, never a confirmed negative - deriving under-escalation is C2's job.
- Local-dev Observe (Settings → Observe) is gated on `app.isPackaged === false` or `FM3000_DEV_OBSERVE=1`, never a user-facing setting. It reads existing session JSONL + `usage_events`; see `docs/dev-observe.md`. It lists three kinds - main, supervision, crew - and is the ONE surface where the word "supervision" renders. `tasks.session_file` is the backend's resume token, not always a path: `src/core/observe/transcriptSource.ts` resolves it per backend (Claude's transcript is the client's own JSONL in `~/.claude`, `src/core/claude/claudeTranscript.ts`; Cursor has none readable), and a selected session is never a blank pane - `transcriptNote` says why when nothing can be read.
- Live mic RMS is a module ref (`src/renderer/src/voice/liveVoiceLevel.ts`), not Zustand. Streaming card bodies are subscribed only by `CardLayer` in `src/renderer/src/app/HomeScreen.tsx`, so they do not re-render Firstmate or VoiceInput.
- The character (captain-approved spec, `firstmate/data/fm3000-character-animation-prototypes-s1/report.md`): `src/renderer/src/character/machine.ts` is an explicit input-reconciled state machine - base states idle|listening|working, one-shot emotes (greet/celebrate/ponder/confused/fidget pool with a 5.6s pretend black hole), and a `busy` parameter that carries the ember INDEPENDENTLY of state (heat is deliberately not in the state targets - listening mid-turn runs hot and cools in place). Attention (voice or text presence) always wins and cuts emotes short; emotes fire only from idle/working and return home through busy; the listening shapeshift keeps two counter-rotating hexagons - the old inner square's vertices sink away by captain's call, so the flat form no longer matches the app icon's three rings. Fleet moments reach the character via `emoteSignal.ts` (task_landed → celebrate; turn_failed / task_finished-failed → confused), a module-ref side channel like liveVoiceLevel - never store state. `machine.test.ts` pins the captain-verified behaviors; don't regress them without a new captain call. The pretend-black-hole fidget's geometry is `src/renderer/src/character/blackhole.ts` (captain's pick from the three-treatment review, `firstmate/data/fm3000-blackhole-emote-proto-s1/report.md`, 2026-09-05): one inclined accretion disk whose far side is lensed over the shadow, Doppler-beamed, with escaping quanta as an explicitly stylized Hawking cue - the physics-vs-license notes in its header are part of the design, keep them honest. It paints an under-layer (halo, shadow, rim) before the wires and an over-layer after, so occlusion is by construction; the emote's envelope, gaze and squint are the shipped ones and the eyes keep their own look over the pointer (PR 60's natural priority). `FirstmateMachine.requestEmote(name, now, variant)` and `pinEmote` exist for tests and review pages only - the product never forces a fidget; `tests/e2e/character-blackhole.spec.ts` reads the emote off the real canvas after making the pool's draw deterministic.
- The Firstmate's working-state glow deliberately diverges from the design skill's `components/mate/Firstmate.jsx` mock (which also predates the eyes and emotes - the app is the character's reference implementation now): the mock sets `ctx.shadowBlur` per primitive, the app composites one blurred mask per character (`src/renderer/src/character/glow.ts`). Same picture, 4-13x cheaper, plus a dpr fix - Canvas2D measures `shadowBlur` in device pixels and ignores the CTM, so glow width must carry an explicit `* dpr`. Do not "re-port the mock verbatim" over it. Derivation and fidelity measurements: `firstmate/data/fm3000-neon-halo-proto-s1/report.md`. The pipeline's first two executions cost 5-10x a warm run (offscreen allocation + Skia blur warmup), so `drawFrame` warms it once on the character's first idle frame (`warmNeonHalo`, erased by the same frame's clear) instead of paying that mid-morph on the first idle->working transition; `glow.test.ts` pins that every warmup stage runs for real.
- Sharp edges already paid for: Pi's `tools` allowlist gates custom tools too (name them or they silently vanish); srcdoc iframes inherit the app CSP, so the frame bridge runs by SHA-256 hash pinned in `src/shared/plugins/bridge.ts` (test-locked to the script text) - and a template with its own script can never ride srcdoc, which is why plugin template mounts are documents the shell serves over `app-frame:` with their own CSP header (`src/main/frames/`); Chromium drops native clicks into sandboxed OOP iframes when the window is hidden - e2e dispatches in-frame clicks; quota fetches run in-process per vault account (`AccountVault.resolveForQuota`; Pi's `getAuth` refreshes OAuth inside the account's store) and never read ambient machine credentials; the preload must bundle its npm deps (`externalizeDeps.exclude`); better-sqlite3 13 is Node-API, one prebuild serves Node and Electron.
- The account broker (rev-7, `docs/architecture.md` §16): provider sign-ins live in per-account stores owned by `AccountVault` (`src/core/pi/accountVault.ts`) - one 0700 dir per account, FM3000 never reads a token, removal cannot touch a sibling. Direct injection only (NO proxy): `CrewmateSpec.accountId` → the account's own `ModelRuntime`. The Firstmate flagship is a Pi account rebindable ONLY at attachment points (app start, explicit pin, exhaustion ladder at idle) - never mid-turn; the real-Pi rebind contract test (`firstmateSession.rebind.contract.test.ts`) gates that path. Backend admission: `ControlProfile` in `src/core/placement/placement.ts` - the Firstmate role requires native steer; followup-queue backends (Cursor) are crewmate-only, and each transport repeats its profile so the supervisor can decide per task.
- Credential health (provider-agnostic, `docs/architecture.md` §16.4): `AccountBackend.health()` / `renew()` is the one owner of "keep every account healthy". `status()` is a projection of health. Pi's `getAuth` is resolve-is-renewal; Claude's delegated ladder lives in `ClaudeAuthBackend.renew`; Cursor answers `unsupported`. `CredentialHealthService` rides the supervisor's 60s tick and renews at `expiresAt - lead` *before* the vendor 401; `fetchQuota`'s `auth.renew` is the reactive 401 caller of the same method. Five-rule contract in `src/core/accounts/credentialHealth.ts`: sign in once; self-heal invisibly; unknown is never absent and a no-UI failure is never a sign-out; `needs_reauth` only from proof (lapsed refresh or a 401 that survived a real renewal); the terminal state is first-class and one-step recoverable. A renew failure degrades honestly, never fabricates health. Do not add a second renewer.
- Every Pi API touchpoint stays behind `src/core/pi/` (Biome `noRestrictedImports` enforces it). Never read `~/.pi`; e2e proves it via a HOME override. User-turn images ride Pi's `PromptOptions.images` / `steer(text, images)` as flat `{ type, data, mimeType }` parts, never as a content array in the text position - Pi's `prompt()` does string work on `text` and crashes on an array (`firstmateSession.realSession.test.ts` pins the shape).
- Every `ModelRuntime` is created by `src/core/pi/modelRuntime.ts`, never `ModelRuntime.create` directly: it owns the live pi.dev catalog policy and its proven static fallback (`docs/architecture.md` §16.3). The trap it exists for: pi's `modelRefreshTimeoutMs` aborts the whole refresh, and the availability pass rides that same signal, so a timed-out catalog fetch otherwise leaves the model picker EMPTY - the factory rebuilds availability offline, and `modelRuntime.test.ts` fails if that rebuild goes away. E2E is kept off `pi.dev` by `PI_OFFLINE=1` in `tests/e2e/launch.ts`. The factory also serves getModel through `withHonestReasoning`: a live def claiming `reasoning: true` whose thinkingLevelMap pins no effort token comes out non-reasoning, because Pi's openai-responses driver (no `supportsReasoningEffort` gate, unlike openai-completions) otherwise passes the session's thinking level through and the provider 400s every turn (grok-build-0.1, captain dogfood 2026-09-01).
- Two model lists, two rules. The routing pool (`availableModels()`) is sign-in gated, then narrowed by the user's slot record (`ModelSlots.routable()`). The quota catalog (`buildModelsCatalog`) is deliberately provider-wide so unmeasurable quota reads as unknown, not zero (`fetchQuota.test.ts`); never add the gate to it. Any "these are my models" surface reads the slot-first view (`ModelSlots.view()`), which is already sign-in gated because it is built from the accounts' own availability snapshots.
- The routing redesign (captain decisions A/B/C, 2026-09-01; builds on PR 40's `withHonestReasoning`, cherry-picked to main by PR 41). Three boundaries now sit around the ladder in `routingEngine.route()`, and each has a single home:
 - **Capability** (`src/core/routing/capability.ts`): a candidate's def is resolved BEFORE it is chosen (`src/core/pi/modelCapability.ts` reads it out of the same runtimes the session will use, so it is the `withHonestReasoning`-corrected def) and skipped with a recorded reason when it cannot carry the turn - images or context. High-slot placement is trusted fully (no reasoning skip). A def no runtime knows is UNKNOWN, not incapable. There is deliberately NO failure/incident ledger; the captain cut it.
 - **Premium** (`PREMIUM_SLOT` / `AUTO_ROUTABLE_SLOTS` in `src/shared/modelSlots.ts`): a fourth slot above high that automatic selection NEVER picks - not in `route()`, not in the consult/supervision walk (`src/core/routing/candidates.ts`, including its uncatalogued tail), not in the flagship derivation. Only an explicit pin reaches one. A premium starter row (`claude-fable-5-1`, `gpt-6-astra`) is pinnable without a settings trip, never auto-picked.
 - **Slots** (`src/core/routing/modelSlots.ts` + `src/shared/modelSlots.ts`): a per-OFFERING record (decision C - the same id can sit in two slots on two providers; never dedupe ids across providers). Seeded from `STARTER_SLOTS` on first activation only; live-catalog newcomers arrive off unless the map names them, and are announced once. Off = in no slot. The fallback ladder is slotted → starter map virtually → the whole signed-in pool at medium: a shortlist is a preference, never a way to brick routing. Pins bypass it - naming a model is its own placement. Per-account control is the account's pause, not a second toggle.
  Every skip and every rung lands in `routing_decisions` / `account_decisions`; that observability is what made the 2026-09-01 dogfood diagnosable, so never quiet it.
- Same-tier routing order: spend priority first (quota-axi ranking semantics - the scope whose paid allowance is most on track to expire unused; a known signal, even negative, outranks an unmeasurable one, and unknown is NEVER zero), then a newer id within the same model line (dotted/dashed version tokens; the line is the id's prefix AND suffix around the version, so gpt-5.6-luna never outranks gpt-5.3-codex-spark) still overrides; unmeasurable candidates keep runway order (`newerId` + the ranked pool in `src/core/routing/routingEngine.ts`; the account pick in `accountPolicy.ts` ranks the same way).
- Quota reliability (captain escalation 2026-09-04, investigation report `fm3000-quota-visibility-diag-s1`). The sensor's job is to be honest about what it established, and to recover from routine expiry without a sign-in. Four rules that must not regress:
  - **The vendor's verdict drives reactive renewal; the tick renews first.** A 401 - and only a 401, never a 403, which is also how a WAF refuses - makes `fetchOneAccount` (`src/core/quota/fetchQuota.ts`) ask `AccountBackend.renew` (`vendor_rejected`), then retry once. The same method is what the supervisor tick calls proactively at `expiresAt - lead`. Claude's delegated ladder (`renewClaudeQuotaAuth`) walks supported non-interactive commands and stops at the first that actually CHANGES the stored credential (`docs/claude-renew-probe.md`). Pi accounts declare resolve-is-renewal: `getAuth` already refreshed. Cursor answers `unsupported`, so a vendor 401 stands.
  - **One owner per credential store, with an ASYMMETRIC priority.** `src/core/claude/claudeStoreLease.ts` is the single answer to "who may spawn the client right now": a crewmate session holds a shared lease for its lifetime and one-shot runs take an exclusive one, with claim and check in the same tick so there is no check-then-spawn window. The priority is the load-bearing part, and it is not symmetric: a **renewal WAITS OUT** an ordinary one-shot run (`runRenewalStoreTask`, bounded) because it is the recovery path, and stands down only for a live SESSION, whose single-use refresh token it must not race; the **status probe gives way** to everything, because its answer already falls back to the account's own store. Making the renewal merely refuse when busy was a real hole - the probe's own polling could stand the app's own recovery down tick after tick, found on a live MacBook tick as `renewal_deferred` and reproduced against the real interfaces in `renewalScheduling.test.ts`. FM3000 owns its sessions, so this is a registry - never a process scan, never a broker.
  - **Not knowing is its own state, and so is recovering.** `quotaProviderViewSchema` carries `ok | auth_required | rate_limited | unavailable | not_measured` plus a sanitized `reason` code and `measuredAt`. `renewal_succeeded` on an `ok` row is the ONE positive trace a renewal leaves - without it an `ok` after a failure is indistinguishable from plain network recovery, so a snapshot could only ever prove recovery had NOT worked; never record it on an ordinary reading that needed no renewal. Only `auth_required` may say "sign in again" or raise the needs_reauth card (CD-3=A: singleton card + Subscriptions CTA + one-step restore via `accounts.signIn`); it is reachable from exactly two proofs - a lapsed refresh token (`refresh_token_lapsed`, `claudeQuota.ts`) or a vendor rejection that SURVIVED a real renewal (`rejected_after_renewal`, `fetchQuota.ts`). A transient miss, a no-interactive-session block, and an unreadable store stay `unavailable` and retryable. `mergeStaleProviders` keeps last-known-good with its age through everything else, dropping windows whose own reset has passed. A no-window fallback is never a success and unknown is never zero.
  - **The credential-and-request layer has real coverage.** `tests/e2e/quota-live-sensor.spec.ts` is the one e2e that does NOT use the fixture seam: it runs the real `createQuotaFetcher` against a local stub of the vendor endpoint (`FM3000_CLAUDE_USAGE_URL`, `FM3000_GROK_USAGE_URL`, `FM3000_CURSOR_USAGE_URL`, dev/e2e-gated exactly like `FM3000_QUOTA_FIXTURE_DIR`). Two provider defects reached the captain twice because that layer had none.
  Grok is METERED since the 2026-09-05 dogfood fix: `providers/grok.ts` reads the consumer credits meter (`grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig`, an UNDOCUMENTED gRPC-web endpoint that can change without notice) with the account's own Pi OAuth token, mirroring the proven quota-axi read - not its browser headers: the meter answers with the bearer, the gRPC-web content type and marker alone, so FM3000 sends nothing that claims to be a browser or another client. `src/core/quota/grpcWeb.ts` is the schema-less reader (framing, trailers, a bounded protobuf field scanner); the field map in grok.ts is reverse-engineered and confirmed against a live capture (`providers/grok.test.ts` carries the bytes). A body the reader does not recognize is `schema_unrecognized`, never a window. A meter refusal (401/403, gRPC 16/7) is NOT a sign-in verdict on its own - whether a Pi-minted xAI token reaches the consumer meter was never established on the captain's account - so the sign-in is probed once (`/v1/models`): alive means the honest disclosed line with `meter_*` as the reason, and only the vendor's own 401 is `auth_required`. `FM3000_GROK_USAGE_URL` is the dev/e2e endpoint override, gated like `FM3000_CLAUDE_USAGE_URL`.
  Cursor is METERED since CD-4=B2 (2026-09-10): `providers/cursor.ts` reads the undocumented DashboardService RPC (`api2.cursor.sh/aiserver.v1.DashboardService/GetCurrentPeriodUsage`, Connect `application/proto`) with the account's own 0600 file-store bearer (`AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE=file`). The endpoint can change without notice; an unrecognised body is `schema_unrecognized`, never a window. A meter 401/403 is not a sign-in verdict on its own - GetMe is probed once; a live GetMe is the disclosed no-window line, and only GetMe's own 401 is `auth_required`. Cursor has no renewal, so `fetchOneAccount` leaves that 401 standing rather than rewriting it as `renewal_unsupported`. Status() still never treats a probe failure as a sign-out (P1b). `FM3000_CURSOR_USAGE_URL` is the dev/e2e override.
- Quota parity (dogfood fix 2026-09-01): `src/shared/quotaSignals.ts` is the ONE home of derived quota math - pace/reserve/burnMultiple, runway projection, spendPriority, per-provider scope bounding - reimplemented clean-room to quota-axi's README semantics (never add quota-axi as a dependency or copy its source; `quotaSignals.test.ts` pins real published readings to 4 decimals). Signals are recomputed from a snapshot's cycle evidence (`resetsAtMs`/`windowSeconds` on windows) at read time, never persisted. Provider rules that must not regress: model/product windows bound only their own scope (never the account-wide min); Copilot windows have NO combined bound (relationships unknown - report nothing, invent nothing); a signed-in account with no readable window renders a disclosed detail line, never a silent blank (`GROK_NO_WINDOW_DETAIL` is the Grok case when the meter answers with nothing readable or refuses a live sign-in - it states what happened on that read, never that the credential cannot expose usage). Claude is SENSED: `src/core/claude/claudeQuota.ts` reads the machine's default login (`.credentials.json` in `~/.claude`, else the bare Keychain item `Claude Code-credentials` - presence-probe first). Only a host `absent` outcome (`errSecItemNotFound`, OSStatus -25300) is absence; a thrown presence-probe or an unparseable value is a named `keychain_*` read failure (`locked` / `unavailable` with `detail` and Retry), never an empty store and never `credential_unavailable` with the reason erased. `keychain_no_interactive_session` stays out of `keychainLocks` so every tick retries (a relaunch fixes it); a decline still holds until Retry. A `demand` refresh chains after an in-flight tick so Retry is not swallowed; a post-rung resolve that cannot read the store is `unreadable`, not `unchanged`. The Keychain VALUE read rides `HostCapabilities.keychain` (CD-5=B: in-process Security.framework, never `/usr/bin/security`) and is requested at account connect/sign-in (`requestKeychainValueAccess` from `ClaudeAuthBackend.login`), the moment a permission prompt is expected. `providers/claude.ts` calls the vendor's OAuth usage endpoint; renewal is delegated to the client, never reimplemented. Pace vocabulary follows quota-axi: "ahead" = burning faster than the reset clock = the WARN state ("behind" is calm) - the pre-parity UI had this inverted; don't bring that back.
- A provider is served by the backend its `PROVIDER_CATALOG` entry names (`src/shared/providers.ts`), and may only serve the `roles` it lists. Claude Max rides its own first-party client because Pi's Anthropic OAuth is refused for third-party clients, is `crewmate`-only, and uses the machine's default `claude login` as its one credential (CD-1=B: one Claude account ever, `binding()` is `{ via: "default-login" }`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` left unset so the client uses the bare Keychain item, unbind does not run `claude auth logout`); the bare `anthropic` Pi provider is still not offered, and leftover Anthropic auth/sessions must not crash the app. Cursor rides its own client for the same reason and is `crewmate`-only too. Adding a backend is a catalog entry plus a registration in `src/core/services.ts` - see `docs/architecture.md` sections 16.1 and 16.2 rather than copying either one.
- Every `@anthropic-ai/*` import stays behind `src/core/claude/`, the same fence Pi has (Biome `noRestrictedImports`). The Claude client is the SDK's own vendored binary (~310MB per darwin arch, both shipped in the universal app) - packaging has not yet been sized for it. `FM3000_CLAUDE_CLI` overrides the path; e2e points it at `tests/e2e/mockClaudeClient.ts`. Two things that binary taught us the expensive way (captain dogfood, packaged build, 2026-09-01):
  - **Never spawn a path inside app.asar.** `child_process.spawn` cannot execute one (only `execFile` is asar-aware), and Electron's asar shim answers `fs.existsSync` for it - so the obvious check passes and the spawn fails ENOTDIR. `resolveClaudeExecutable` (`src/core/claude/claudeCli.ts`) maps an in-archive path to the `app.asar.unpacked` copy and returns only a file really on disk; `electron-builder.yml` says `asarUnpack` for it out loud instead of leaning on smart-unpack, and `tests/release-contract.test.ts` pins both. Any future vendored binary needs the same treatment.

# Project agent memory

This file is the project's committed home for project-intrinsic agent knowledge: build, test, release, architecture, and sharp-edge notes that should travel with the code.

## What this project is

Firstmate 3000 is a local-only Electron desktop app: a calm AI first-officer that routes work to the user's own LLM subscriptions (Codex, Copilot, Grok, Claude Max, Cursor, Kimi, OpenRouter, ...). No SaaS, no hosted backend, no account system from us. Product vision, interaction model, and constraints: `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/readme.md`.

## Standing product principle (captain, 2026-08-17)

FM3000 is the most advanced agent harness, but it aggressively hides that complexity from the end user. The user interacts with just the main Firstmate agent and a few settings - nothing else. The fewer concepts we expose, the better. Accounts, harnesses, crewmate transports, quota routing, and rebinding are machinery; the surfaces a person touches stay calm. Concretely: the sign-in flow and the Subscriptions tab never expose the "harness" technicality - they speak only of providers, accounts (labeled by the user), and quota. An e2e assertion enforces the wording.

## Design system (mandatory)

All UI work MUST follow the project skill `firstmate-3000-design` (`.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/`). It owns every visual and interaction rule: tokens, type, color, motion, components, character rendering, tone of copy. Never re-invent brand rules in code; if a rule is missing, extend the skill first, then implement. The package is offline-complete (fonts and mock runtime vendored; see its readme "Offline completeness").

- Tokens: `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/tokens/*.css` - consume these, never hardcode values they define.
- Click-through mock of the whole app: serve the skill dir over HTTP (any static server), open `ui_kits/firstmate/index.html`. Voice states trigger on a real right-⌥ keydown.

## Architecture and implementation

The architecture is **decided** (captain sign-off 2026-08-13, decision record in `docs/architecture.md` §14 - do not relitigate). Implementers start from `docs/implementation-plan.md`, which orders the build into phases with acceptance checks and names the house reference repos to mirror (Pi SDK, hi-bit, baby-menu, pi-launcher). If reality contradicts a recorded decision, escalate with `needs-decision` instead of improvising. Current build status vs the plan: `docs/mvp-status.md`.

## Working on the code

- Green gate on every commit: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence && pnpm test`, then `pnpm build && pnpm exec playwright test` for the e2e suite. The adherence lint runs the design skill's `_adherence.oxlintrc.json` through ESLint FlatCompat (current oxlint cannot execute its selector rules); its raw-px/hex rules are warn-level by the skill's own design.
- Standing CI rule (PR 8): CI green only if every check on the exact head commit SHA reports status=completed and conclusion=success (use `gh pr checks`). One green `checks` job never suffices while `package-smoke` or others pend/fail. Never treat old SHAs as authoritative for the current head.
- E2E runs are hermetic and windowless: `tests/e2e/launch.ts` gives each app a throwaway userData and HOME (`FM3000_USER_DATA_DIR` keeps the window hidden - captain directive), fake media devices (no macOS mic prompt), a mock OpenAI-compatible provider wired through app-scoped `models.json` (`tests/e2e/mockProvider.ts`), and faked voice-model readiness (opt out with `voiceModelReady: false`). Quota fixtures ride `FM3000_QUOTA_FIXTURE_DIR`. Claude credentials seed into that HOME's `.claude` (`prepareHome`), never a per-account vault store.

It stamps migration 16's nullable `missed_escalation`/`missed_note`/`missed_at` on the task's newest routine `supervision_outcomes` row (or a named `#id` from `supervision_log`), write-once, `routine`-only, and captain-turn gated by the same wake stamp `remember` uses - the label's value is that the captain confirmed it, so the agent cannot manufacture one on a scheduled or supervision wake. Refusals are tool text, never throws. No card, no setting, no user surface.
- The retrospective miss deriver (PoC-2 capture C2, `scripts/derive-miss-candidates.ts`, `docs/miss-deriver.md`) is an OFFLINE tables-only scan: for every `supervision_outcomes` `routine` verdict it looks forward in a window (default 24h) for a later captain verdict, a host-written `turn_failed` / task-failure wake, a captain-resolved card, or a captain steer/interrupt on that task, and emits weak candidate-miss JSONL. Never writes C3's `missed_escalation`/`missed_note`/`missed_at`. Inputs are parameters (`--db`/`--user-data`/`--window-hours`) so a MacBook-exported `firstmate.db` runs identically.
